prompts.A:
Use case: product-mockup / stylized-concept.
Asset: physical wood frame for the existing Legend of the Five Rings Emperor Edition digital playmat. This is an art-direction concept sheet for later measured Blender construction and Godot camera validation, NOT a screenshot of an implemented game.
Reference image 1 is the APPROVED playmat artwork: use its exact navy/charcoal textile, quiet open centre, warm gold cloud/pine/landscape ornament concentrated along the left and right edges, and its broad 1672:941 landscape proportions. Map the reference art naturally onto the cloth insert. Preserve composition and relative ornament positions, do not redesign the mat. The new physical rim REPLACES the thin painted outer rim; never show two nested picture frames. The full cloth play area remains unobstructed.
Output: a beautifully art-directed, photorealistic AAA game asset presentation, landscape 16:10, high detail. Same layout for both variants: upper two thirds a large complete shallow rectangular playmat/frame from a gentle elevated three-quarter angle, its long side horizontal and entire outline visible with modest margins; lower third two beautifully lit larger close-up panels showing the near-left corner join and the inset cloth meeting the inner wood bevel. Restrained dark-charcoal neutral backdrop, no room or table legs. Rim physically narrow (roughly 25–30 mm top width on a 1.8 m × 1.013 m outer footprint), 25–30 mm deep, 3–4 mm softened bevel, cloth flush or only 2 mm recessed so cards can move easily.
Lighting: warm grazing lamplight with soft cool fill, enough exposure to read dark wood grain and actual textile, natural restrained specular response, no dramatic glow, no thick fog or bloom. Wood sides need real depth and a grounded shadow. Show honest buildable material detail rather than fantasy sculptural excess.
No cards, no counters, no UI, no clan emblems, no animals or statues, no lettering in Japanese, no candles/props. Decorative details stay entirely within the wood rim. Avoid oversized filigree, wide rails, jewel-like buttons, chrome, cheap plastic gloss, modern desk metal, decorative elements entering the cloth.
Tiny restrained ivory serif labels only; title in a small weathered uppercase calligraphic face at top left; captions "CORNER JOIN" and "CLOTH / WOOD" below the two close-ups. Do not spend image space on paragraphs or swatches.
Variant A. Title exactly: "A · WORN BLACK LACQUER". Refined Japanese lacquered dark hardwood, near-black top with deep warm brown showing through only at hand-worn bevels and small edge chips. Quiet long grain beneath the lacquer, satin sheen rather than piano gloss. A single hairline of irregular worn antique-gold inlay tracks just outside the inner bevel. Only a very small incised gold corner turn, inspired by the existing mat's corner ornament, fully confined to the narrow rim. Precise mitered corner construction, softly aged outer edge and subtle shadow gap against cloth. Controlled, dignified and time-worn, closely related to the game's approved worn black lacquer menus. The wood must still read as wood, not a metal gold picture frame. The close-up is exquisite: uneven lacquer wear, pore structure, tiny gold loss, smooth hand-polished edges.

Variant B. Title exactly: "B · SMOKED WOOD & BRONZE". Dark smoked brown Japanese hardwood with visibly more natural straight wood grain than variant A, low satin oil finish and gently rounded worn outer bevels. Slightly warmer brown, still dark enough to belong with the deep navy/gold game aesthetic. The structural joints are subtle exposed timber joinery at each corner, reinforced by very small thin antique-bronze corner fittings recessed FLUSH into the wood surface, with a restrained engraved cloud-line detail. Bronze is dark patinated with warm worn edges, no shiny bolts or industrial rivets. No continuous metallic perimeter stripe, no large ornamental metal plates. The contrast comes from beautiful solid wood grain, sober aged joinery and four quiet bronze details. Grounded, tactile and campaign-worn, still elegant enough for a samurai's war table. At the cloth seam show a precise shallow seat with a tiny contact shadow, no raised lip blocking cards.
